22259.d:
Geckos are small, mostly carnivorous lizards that have a wide distribution, found on every continent except Antarctica. Belonging to the infraorder Gekkota, geckos are found in warm climates throughout the world. They range from 1.6 to 60 centimetres (0.6 to 23.6 inches).

Geckos are unique among lizards for their vocalisations, which differ from species to species. Most geckos in the family Gekkonidae use chirping or clicking sounds in their social interactions. Tokay geckos (Gekko gecko) are known for their loud mating calls, and some other species are capable of making hissing noises when alarmed or threatened. They are the most species-rich group of lizards, with about 1,500 different species worldwide.[1] The New Latin gekko and English 'gecko' stem from the Indonesian-Malay gēkoq, which is imitative of sounds that some species make

Grayscale, Hold the Line, and Mondrian walk into a bar. The bartender looks up and says, "What is this, some kind of art project?"

Grayscale responds, "No, we're just here for a drink."

Hold the Line adds, "But we can definitely add some color to the place if you want."

Mondrian chimes in, "I prefer to keep things simple and stick to the basics."

The bartender shakes his head and says, "I'll be the judge of that. What can I get you all?"

Grayscale orders a Guinness, Hold the Line asks for a gin and tonic, and Mondrian asks for a glass of white wine.

The bartender serves up the drinks and says, "That will be $15.50, please."

Grayscale pulls out a twenty-dollar bill and hands it to the bartender, saying, "Keep the change."

The bartender thanks him and says, "Thanks, Grayscale. You always know how to liven up the place."

Hold the Line raises his glass and says, "Cheers to that!"

Mondrian nods and clinks glasses with the others, and the three of them enjoy their drinks and the rest of their evening at the bar.

22262.d:
All through the town, people were preparing for the holiday season. As the snow began to fall gently outside, people settled in for the night, dreaming of sugarplums and presents. But little did they know, something sinister was stirring in the snowy night.

A group of interdimensional monsters were hatching a plan. They had been watching the humans for some time, and they had decided that they wanted to experience the joys of the winter season for themselves. They decided to transport themselves to earth in snowglobes, and hide among the decorations in the homes of the humans.

On Christmas morning, as the humans woke up to open their presents, the monsters would emerge from their hiding places and spread chaos and destruction throughout the town.

But things didn't go as planned for the monsters. As they arrived on earth and hid themselves in the snowglobes, they began to feel a strange warmth in their hearts. They watched as the humans celebrated the season with love and joy, and they realized that they wanted to be a part of it.

Something very different happens in homes without warmth, but we won't talk about that.

Collection details:
- Backgrounds: 22 equirectangular environments and 42 holiday pattern environments
- Globe base: 24 color types
- Monsters: 44
- Naughty Monsters are much more frequent, Nice Monsters are rare
- Snow can be stormy or calm, and ends up in bumpy or smooth piles
- One song "Greensleeves" performed and recorded by the collection author

22265.d:
The "Radials" collection is a series of generative art pieces that seek to capture the fleeting moments of blurry, dreamlike visions. Using bold, vibrant colors and swirling, abstract forms, each piece in the collection is unique, as the generative algorithms used to create them produce endless variations and permutations.

The goal of the "Radials" collection is to invite viewers to let go of their preconceived notions and to allow themselves to be drawn into a world of blurry, dreamlike visions. The pieces in this collection are meant to be experienced on an emotional level, rather than being analyzed or dissected intellectually. As such, they provide a unique opportunity for viewers to tap into their own subconscious minds and to explore the hidden corners of their imagination.

22291.d:
Laboratory of curious graphic studies.

Imagine an old file found near Weinar, containing the graphic research of a geometry enthusiast...

A geometric figure with each side composed of a certain number of points (between 10 and 100) undergoes a rotation.

A grain, or "granularity"  brings a pencil effect that gives the illusion of old archives rescued from a secret's Bauhaus laboratory. Old illustrations whose paper would have undergone the damage of time.

Features:
- Paper: yellowed, cracked and dry most of the time, but there were a few pages found with the marks of time bleached out.
- Basic shape type: Polygons, sometimes stars. 
- Symmetry: Perfectly symmetrical geometrical shapes, but not always!
- x' and y' : parameters for the deformation, based on the Lissajous equations. The value for x is very often 1, the other values are totally random between 1 and 10, but it seems that there are 30 too.
- Length Loop : Time to draw the shape, usually 800 frames but we have seen some at 400 frames and others at 1600. 
- Granularity: 100 levels of granularity.
- Sides or branches : Mostly between 3 and 5.
- Points per sides or branches : around 50 (Gaussian Standard Deviation : 15).

Controls:
[ENTER] to pause or restart playback.
[s] to download the image*.

*The maximum print size is limited by the resolution and power of your computer. See https://www.fxhash.xyz/article/how-to-print-generative-art to print at high resolutions.

Made with the javascript framework P5.js

Jérôme Mercier - @generativePunk - https://www.pizza-punk.com 
December, 2022

22331.d:
Set-square is an instrument in the form of a right triangle, used to draw angles and perpendiculars, in Portuguese we call it Esquadro.

When developing this study, I reflected on the action of order and disorder of alignments, the need I feel when instinctively seeking order and at the same time learning to live with disorder. Programming was like learning to draw all over again, and in Esquadros I try to extrapolate this issue by using simple geometric shapes and slightly playful colors, portraying this phase of starting over.

Esquadros displays some simple variations: density, palettes, a little clutter in some pieces and some inverted colors.

Appreciate the simple shapes and colors that life offers us, even in the midst of a lot of order and disorder. This is my genesis for Fx Hash.

Key controls:

k : save png
l : show pallete label

Artwork by Zizou, @Zizoutez.

Made with p5.js and <3

Many birds fly in foggy weather. Migratory waterfowl generally do not let fog stop them from continuing their journeys, although it may slow them down a bit. Local songbirds know their territories like you know your home. They can usually get from place to place within their “home” in the fog with little difficulty. If fog is quite a rare event (and has always been rare) in a particular region, you might find the fog reduces some bird activity, as they will have always lived in a region with good, clear visibility.

Remember, too, that most birds have vision capabilities that allow them to see further into the violet and ultraviolet spectrum, so the scattering of blue light that confuses human vision is not near the problem for most birds.

22345.d:
The circle is an amazing strange geometrical form, it is by far the simplest geometric shape that exists, you might disagree with that, but actually, there are hundreds of pages long of mathematical proof of why it is, it's called "The Poincaré conjecture" this is one of the most difficult problems that stayed unsolved 20th century to prove that a circle is the simplest shape until it was demonstrated in 2003. When you see a drawing circle, it's a circle in two dimensions, right? What would it look like if it was in three dimensions, it's a sphere; same shape but more dimensions, but it's still the simplest kind of shape that exists in three dimensions. No matter how many dimensions you add, according to the Poincaré conjecture, it will always be the simplest shape. Even though it seems straightforward, there are extremely profound difficult problems within it.

The astonishing thing about circles is what we can do with them, particularly by using the majestic number π and connecting straight and curved lines using topological or geometrical functions. "The esoteric form" project is an example of how a circle can take on countless shapes and unusual, vibrant forms while also being simple and complex at the same time.

Press [s] to save captured image to png (2200px x 2200px)
Wait a moment it takes a while to be rendered (Up to 30s)

22371.d:
We cannot compose life, at best we hum along to the melodies that life has been played in front of us. Looking back at the scores of our lives, the notations are never neatly noted, but fully felt.  Rewinding the songs of life are our memories, whether sad, happy, angry, or melancholy. It is not clear whether I am dreaming or awake, but our songs all do end. 

In this final drop (for ?), I have reused the first ever class calligraphy(){} I have written from my genesis drop “Nothing comes from nothing”. As time passes, 10 drops later, across almost to the year, I am grateful for the progress I have made, as an artist, and more importantly as a human. After all, what is behind the code of generative art is a human being. 

Scores of music, scrolls of calligraphy, calendar or diary, notating life, time passes, and changes are inevitable. Sometimes we sing louder in laughter and joy, sometimes we scribble in uneasiness, sometimes we just get lost in neon lights. Life goes on. You and me, all the same and yet different.  

There are too many friend artists, friend collectors, fxhash team members, to thank for helping me through this journey. I would like to pay homage to Rudxane in this work, who has taken me under his wings, mentoring and encouraging me in art as well as showing me some degen stuff on the side:-). This homage is not copy-minting, or copying of styles, which I do not have the coding skills to do so even if I wanted to. But it is the influence of taste in many works of Rudxane. In a vague but agreeable taste, I present to you Life has no scores. 

What I was taught was disrupted, and grid studies left unfinished, and oh do we have a BINGO?

22383.d:
It may appear as an indecipherable map to some. To others, it may present itself as a cross section of an underground cave. Or maybe an uncanny landscape of volcanic activity, a diagram of geological strata, or even something else entirely. Some vague structure may also appear; is it the remains of an ancient civilization? Or perhaps a glimpse into our own tomorrow?

In "Agharta", I sought to create a generative work that could invite the viewer to explore the depths of their imagination and uncover hidden structures within the seemingly chaotic composition. The idea came to me when I was exploring Simplex noise and pixel displacement in Cables. I was surprised by the emergent structures that appeared when some set of parameters paired with the right texture. 

The title of the piece references the mythical underground world said to be located at the earth's core. This idea of hidden depths and secret worlds within the earth resonates with the abstract and enigmatic nature of the result generated by the noise. Imagery of landscape, vague structures, or geological features may appear but never stand out on its own; it exists in a state of constant flow and intersection as if viewed from another dimension. And just like the myth itself that bring up numerous theories that doesn’t necessarily connected to each other, it hints at that idea of an elusive imagined realm while never actually represent it completely.



=========

Controls:

[1] Set resolution to 716 x 1024px (default)

[2] Set resolution to 1433 x 2048px

[3] Set resolution to 2688 x 3840px

* The presets above are suitable for screen viewing up to 4k screen resolution. To set a custom resolution for printing and other purpose, add &res=[desired resolution] at the end of the URL. It will set the height of the image, and the width will be calculated automatically at 0.7 ratio. For example to get a resolution of 4911 x 7016px (about the size of A2 paper), add &res=7016 as URL parameter.

[Scroll/pinch] to zoom and drag to pan

[r] or [zoom out to max] Reset position

[c] Capture a screenshot of the current state at rendered resolution


Notes:

* This project use shaders that relies on GPU. Hi-res output may slow down your device. Since it also utilize GPU instance for thumbnail rendering, expect longer time for every iterations to be signed by fx(hash).

* If 'glitching' occurs or the composition behaves differently at different resolution, just refresh the page to reset it (except for the thin lines, which are always drawn at approximately 1 pixel, so expect it to vary at different resolution).

Made with cables.gl, a node-based webgl environment

XALTED 2022

22391.d:
3 Armonografos Sobre Figuras / 3 Harmonographs on Shapes

"If I had to choose, the harmonograph is my preferred mechanism for making gen art"

The composition works with three harmonographs vertically distributed with 2 pendulums each that draw on black and white shapes. It is a game between the positive and the negative.

Steps-Layers:

1 - White or black background
2 - Draw shape 1 (triangle or Circle or Rectangle) with the opposite tone to the background.
3 - Draw shape 2 (triangle or Circle or Rectangle) same tone as the background.
4 - Draw the 3 Harmonographs. The (inverted) tones depend on the tones of the shapes and background.
5 - Cutting / glitch effect. Vertical and horizontal.
6 - Symmetries X or Y or XY or none are applied.
7 - Rectangles are cut again (yes/no)

// ---

"Si tuviese que elegir, el armonografo es mi mecanismo preferido para hacer arte generativo"

La composición trabaja con tres armónografos de 2 péndulos distribuídos verticalmente que dibujan sobre figuras en blanco y negro. Es un juego entre positivos y negativos.

A kaleidoscope (/kəˈlaɪdəskoʊp/) is an optical instrument with two or more reflecting surfaces (or mirrors) tilted to each other at an angle, so that one or more (parts of) objects on one end of these mirrors are shown as a regular symmetrical pattern when viewed from the other end, due to repeated reflection.

These reflectors are usually enclosed in a tube, often containing on one end a cell with loose, colored pieces of glass or other transparent (and/or opaque) materials to be reflected into the viewed pattern. Rotation of the cell causes the motion of the materials, resulting in an ever-changing view being presented.

A person cannot always evaluate something by one example. After drying one song from an album, you can't say "cool album".

What if the album is one story? Do you understand what I mean? I cut off different patterns with the same base colors and already created a whole story.

Sometimes by changing the angle of view, you change everything you see. Perhaps if you saw my usual artwork, you would not notice the essence of generativity without these colors.

ARTIST:  Geneva Lee Robles

MEDIUM: This work is an image composition with generative elements. The underlying image is a handmade linocut print whose parts were deconstructed via powerpoint, and pixel arrays processed via p5js. In this debut collection, the artist utilizes traditional and digital mediums to convey the feeling of simplicity and chaos.           

THE ART: “The Weight” is an award winner for the New York Foundation for the Arts (NYFA) NFT Award Program.  Inspired by bridging traditional art and technology, subsequent iterations of the work utilize coded generative elements to enhance its story.  

EXHIBITION: “THE WEIGHT” is a part of “Demystifying NFTs: The Award Exhibition”, on display in Voxel’s Metaverse at the BRIDGE ++ space from December 15th - December 31st, 2022, curated by Laura Ó Reilly and presented by NYFA. 

BEHIND THE ART: Weight is a recurring theme in the artist’s work, depicted metaphorically as she revisits the emotional turbulence she experienced as a child of Chinese and Puerto Rican descent, raised in a home of heroin addiction and chaos. The weight tells the story of the heaviness we carry in life, and our resilience to keep going in spite of its persistence.  

ABOUT THE ARTIST:  Geneva Lee Robles is an interdisciplinary artist, living in New York City.  She was born in the Bronx and raised in Brooklyn, NY, during a tumultuous period in the 1980s.  Her work attempts to capture the emotional turbulence one is feeling, when no one is watching. She explores themes of loneliness within one's self and their relationships.  She is inspired by integrating traditional forms of art and pushing the envelope of what's possible through technology.

"Citric" is a generative art piece that features irregular circles made with Perlin noise to represent different citrus fruits. Curved shapes with fill represent citrus slices, and their electric colors reflect the fruits' flavors.

The artist explores the concept of generating random shapes and colors using computer algorithms in this work. Using Perlin noise allows each circle to have a unique, random shape, reflecting the variability and complexity of nature.

The electric colors used in the piece also play a crucial role in representing the flavors of the citrus fruits. Bright red represents the acidic taste of an orange, intense green represents the tartness of a lemon, and bright yellow represents the sweet flavor of a grapefruit.

In short, "Citric" is a work that blends computer algorithms and color to create a visual representation of citrus fruits and their flavors. The piece invites the viewer to reflect on the relationship between technology and nature, and how these two elements can be merged in generative art.

Digital Gardens are places of magic and wonder, where you can connect with your inner nature and take a deep breath. Digital Gardens are a refuge from the world outside. A sanctuary for the mind, body, and soul. But they are also a place of play and exploration. It is a space where you can let your imagination run wild, creating and discovering new things.
Digital Gardens brings to life the minimalistic essence of Detegus’ art and the abstract and rational art of Alfredo Boaron.
The gardens are generated from a recursive function dividing the space at each iteration with a proportion that follows the Fibonacci succession and randomly stops after some iterations. At each recursion the canvas is divided into two pieces following the proportion of two consecutive Fibonacci numbers [1 to 144].
The minimalistic visual effect is then personalized by the palettes of 15 artists who embraced the invitation to give their personal contribution to the collection. The palette name and the author name is displayed in the features along with the Fibonacci numbers ratio, the colors number vs the total palette color number, the background color, the total number of rectangles and the depth level of recursion achieved by the algorithm.
Immerse yourself in this generative project, inspired by geometrism and abstract expressionism. 
Lose yourself in the beauty of a digital garden.

The Visual Code is a collection of generative art that celebrates the jazzy, dynamic visuals inspired by Wassily Kandinsky, Jackson Pollock, Kazimir Malevich, Joan Miro and The Dave Brubeck Quartet's music.

Each piece uniquely expresses the artist's creativity and technical skill, showcasing the beauty and complexity of computer-generated visuals.

As a codegen artist, I am constantly in awe of the boundless potential of generative art. The ability to create unique, one-of-a-kind pieces using code is truly fascinating to me.

Generative art allows for a level of artistic expression that is simply not possible with traditional mediums. Using algorithms and mathematical principles allows for creating complex, dynamic visuals that are constantly evolving and changing.

What I find particularly interesting about generative art is its focus on the creation process. Rather than simply producing a static, finished product, the artist is more concerned with the journey and the process of creating the art. This allows for experimentation and exploration that is impossible in more traditional forms of art.

In my own work, I strive to push the boundaries of generative art and explore new possibilities. I constantly experiment with different algorithms and techniques to create something new and unique.

I am excited to continue learning and growing as an artist and to see where my passion for generative art will take me.

The collection is a tribute to the art of coding and its endless possibilities for artistic expression. From mesmerizing geometric patterns to pulsating colour fields, each piece in the collection is a testament to the endless potential of code as a medium for artistic creation.

Previous collectors are automatically on the reserve list for this exclusive collection. This is a rare opportunity to own a piece of generative art that captures the imagination and celebrates the beauty of code.

I asked OpenAI chatGPT to "please create p5.js code to evolve a form in 3d, webgl" to see what would happen, as I'm exploring themes such as extinction and evolution in my specture project

It created a starter shape, in 2d (not WEBGL). so I tweaked its code in evolveForm(), merged it with my algorithms and made this as an evolution composition study, exploring how coding with AI could work going forwards. it was interesting to see the AI had added some dummy code which didn't do anything (removed), and needed to be tweaked to get it to draw at all. it made basic shapes, but I like the overall composition in fullscreen mode. some of the negative shapes are interesting, and would be good to paint, so it's worthwhile as an idea generator. 

merged with my code, it does start to look like some of my earlier specture drawings, so it will be interesting in future to see where the line is between AI code and personal code - in this case with a mix of human + machine, the human parts still come to the fore

Symmetrical design is an aesthetic that incorporates the sense of beauty arising from the use of symmetry. 
Symmetry, in mathematics and other fields, is a type of object in which there's a correspondence between each position along a straight line and its counterpart across that line.

The word symmetry can also mean bilateral or having two sides as with some objects such as a sphere, disk or rectangle where all angles on one side are mirrored on the opposite side.

Considering the physical makeup of a work of art, color and symmetry are two elements that are frequently found in pieces. Color is typically introduced by the artist to create contrast and to set the mood of the piece. Symmetry is created mostly through the use of circles and angles. These elements can be used creatively in a variety of works to convey specific messages or emotions.

These two elements are often used together in artwork to create a sense of optimism and uniqueness. However, they are also combined in negative ways to create artwork that can be disturbing, even disturbing to the artist. In short, it is not always easy to determine what is good and what is bad, since both colors and symmetry can have a positive or negative outcome.

Pixel World Map is a work of art. It is an artistic expression of what the artist believes to be a small part of the world in relation to themselves at this time.
The map is made through a pixel art, an image made up of individual pixels-one after the other-to reflect their perspective on how they see things.

Creating pixel art is an interesting way to express yourself and show your personality by using colors and shapes.

The map was made through a pixel art, an image made up of consecutive pixels-one after another-to reflect their perspective on how they see things.

An ancient civilization had conquered the stars, building huge monoliths to harness their energy. These mega structures now lie in decay, as their lights begin to dim. What happened to these civilizations? We may never know. We can only bear witness to their ends.

The code for "Dying of the Lights" explores the effect of heredity on structure and color. The base data structure is a quadtree in which child nodes inherit properties from its parent. The evolution of each node depends on the structure of the paren, and not all nodes will survive. The structure is then exploded into their final resting place as they slowly orbit the star.

The piece can be animated by hitting "Space" to slowly watch the Dying of the Light. Performance of the animation depends on the complexity of each piece, and the technical specifications of the device.

The viewer can also control the frame depth and color of the final display, as well as show / hide several additional easter eggs in the details.

Controls:
[UP / DOWN] - Adjust frame depth
[LEFT / RIGHT] - Adjust frame color
[D] - Show / hide details
[SPACE] - Animate

*Higher resolution images can be generated by adding &x=[width]&y=[height] behind the url. Larger images may not be rendered well on devices with less memory.

Common sizes at 300dpi: 
A4 = 2490 x 3510
Letter = 2550 x 3300

22484.d:
Many people today may find wonder what exactly is happening to us as we orbit and move around our planet. Some might assume that there’s not much in the way of a reason, others might assume that humans are just being lulled into complacency by having their every need met and be self-absorbed in technology. Or maybe those assumptions are wrong, but for those who know about something called Chaos Theory, it is possible - at least in theory - that we are living in the very beginning moments of a process of change which will pop up from nowhere to take over everything as time goes on.

Some would call it a surprise, but I don’t think a surprise is the right word. In fact, I think that it’s closer to bad luck than anything else. Those of us who know about Chaos Theory know that it’s even possible for a small change at the beginning of the universe to result in the formation of vastly different universes and some where we humans don’t even exist.

Now, this is not something like one person acting differently or changes in other people around that one person. It’s not the butterfly effect. It’s more like there were two people and it was 50-50 to either one of them doing something and then, suddenly, one of those people wasn’t there. How would the other person react? Would they take away a piece of food, or maybe that person wouldn’t have said a particular word at a particular time? In either case, even if it was a tiny tiny difference - I mean, who knows what someone did in the past to make this happen - there would be no way for us to know now that that tiny change decided what kind of universe we live in now and what our lives will be like tomorrow.

How would you feel? Would you think it was bad luck or good luck, or something else? Chances are, you’re going to feel the same way. And don’t think I don’t know what you are thinking of doing if the world was to end and there’d be nobody around but you.

Of course there are people who may have thought about doing something when they came across this article. Maybe people will assume that I am crazy for making these claims - which is fine as long as people assume that I am crazy in general. When things like this happen to us all at once, it is really hard for us to make sense of it all.

This work continues the previous exploration seen in the 🪷🪷🪷🪷🪷 series.

In this work I am exploring a variety of different sonic and visual properties.

Rotation, movement, dimensionality, layering, and sound continue to be important elements of this work.

The visuals are inspired by various sources, such as the beginning of the universe, electromagnetic waves, rotational energy, etc.

The previous work built in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript has been ripped out to allow for experimentation with p5.js code.

It has morphed to accommodate the visuals, adding elements of space, motors, and rotation. As with the previous three generative projects, these soundtracks play for an infinite amount of time.

Playback is possible on a reasonably powered device, but this work is pushing limits, so it may best be enjoyed in the future when you can have access to a more powerful device.

Hypnagogia is the experience of the transitional state from wakefulness to sleep.
Mental phenomena that may occur during this "threshold consciousness" phase include hallucinations, lucid thought, lucid dreaming, and sleep paralysis.

Phosphenes, the entoptic hallucinations, that manifest during hypnagogia appear to the visual cortex as geometric patterns and seemingly archetypal forms. 
This work raises the question of whether these are learned patterns or inherent in the mind itself.

• press 'p' to pause the generation
• press 's' to save the image

Some drawings may be slow, some fast. 
Be patient and find the right hallucination.

Done during sleepless nights with p5.js

22492.d:
Vanilla JS + SVG
November 2022

Edition of 365

The starting point for this piece was an attempt to simulate the effect of dropping coloured inks or paints onto wet or dry paper ("blots") by combining mixed gradients and various levels of svg filters. I then added stroke and fine line drawings to the blots and played around with rotation and opacity and leaving blanks in the grids. 

The results range from minimal smooth circles, sometimes fading away into the background, to noisy splashes or clouds.

The defined features of the project are:

Blot palettes: 9+n (1 is generated randomly)
Blotting paper: 6 colours
Blot grid: 5 layouts (1x1, 3x3, 5x5, 10x10, 20x20)
Blot stroke: true/false
Blot blanks: true/false
Blotted lines: true/false
Blotulence! (extra turbulence): true/false

To save a PNG file, press "P" or save an SVG by pressing "S"

This project has been tested and works in Chrome, Brave, Edge and Firefox (a little slower on the latter, so please be patient). It does not work in Safari or on IOS at this time.
